newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament passes Arrangements Law.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament passes Arrangements Law.

text.p: Israel's parliament on Tuesday evening approved the government's Economic Arrangements Law by a 59-43 vote and will begin debate on the 1997 Budget Law this evening.
Parliament agreed to a Treasury plan to reduce benefits going to newly demobilised soldiers and to delay implementing a longer school day for another three years as a means of cutting spending.

On Monday, however, legislators turned down a Treasury plan to cancel a special half-point tax credit for working women. Cancelling the credit would have raised 270 million shekels the Treasury needs to meet its deficit target.
Treasury officials said they would seek to fill the gap over the next few weeks with new measures.
The ministry is seeking about seven billion shekels in spending cuts and new revenues in order to keep the bduget deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product next year.
The Arrangements Law encompasses changes to the law needed to implement the budget. Debate on the 1997 budget bill is scheduled to being a 1800 GMT and end early Wednesday morning.
